  comms-minio-init:
    profiles: ["comms-media"]
    # `minio/mc`, pinned. The published release image is built from upstream `Dockerfile.release`
    # on `ubi9/ubi-micro`: it DOES carry a shell (`/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`) and coreutils, so this
    # script can run in it — what it does NOT carry is `sed`, `awk`, `grep` or `envsubst`. That is
    # the real constraint, and it is why init.sh does its substitution with bash builtins.
    #
    # The untagged image was the bug this pin fixes: an operator pulling `minio/mc:latest` gets
    # whatever `mc` the base image ships, and the alias-stdin behaviour init.sh depends on is
    # release-specific. Pin to the release that behaviour was measured against.
    #
    # init.sh checks for `mc` on PATH and exits 127 with a message if the pin ever regresses to an
    # image without the client.
    image: minio/mc:RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z
    container_name: comms-minio-init
    depends_on:
      comms-minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${FLEET_COMMS_MINIO_ROOT_USER:-}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${FLEET_COMMS_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}
      FLEET_COMMS_MEDIA_BUCKET: ${FLEET_COMMS_MEDIA_BUCKET:-comms-journal}
      FLEET_COMMS_MEDIA_ACCESS_KEY: ${FLEET_COMMS_MEDIA_ACCESS_KEY:-}
      FLEET_COMMS_MEDIA_SECRET_KEY: ${FLEET_COMMS_MEDIA_SECRET_KEY:-}
    # ⚠️ `/bin/bash`, not `/bin/sh`. The bucket-name substitution in init.sh uses
    # `${var//pattern/replacement}`, which a POSIX `sh` rejects with "Bad substitution" (measured on
    # dash 0.5.12). `minio/mc`'s `/bin/sh` is bash, so this happens to work unforced — say it in the
    # entrypoint anyway, so the interpreter is a stated choice and not an accident of the base image.
    # See the header of deploy/comms-minio-init/init.sh.
    entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "/init/init.sh"]
    volumes:
      - ./deploy/comms-minio-init:/init:ro
    # `restart: on-failure` is a RETRY, not a repair loop: the script is idempotent (bucket
    # --ignore-existing, user add updates in place, policy create overwrites), so a transient
    # failure — MinIO still settling, a network blip — converges on the next attempt.
    #
    # The one failure it cannot fix is a bad pin: if `mc` is ever missing from this image, init.sh
    # exits 127 and restarts forever. That is deliberate. This service is a one-shot, so it is the
    # ONLY place the root credential is used after the server starts; `restart: "no"` would let it
    # stay dead and silently leave the scoped runtime user with no policy — the exact Access Denied
    # failure this whole job exists to prevent. `logging: driver: none` below is what stops the
    # loop from filling the disk, and the symptom is loud: `docker ps` shows the restart count.
    restart: on-failure
    networks:
      - comms-media
    logging:
      driver: "none"
